statement.p: Find the mass of the solid bounded by the xy-plane, yz-plane, xz-plane, and the plane (x/3)+(y/3)+(z/9) = 1, if the density of the solid is given by \delta (x,y,z)=x + 2 y.

static.solution:
z = 9 - 3 x - 3 y. Note that the projection of this into the xy-plane is the triangular region below y = 3 - x.
The mass of the volume is then M = \int_R \delta\,dV = \int_0^3\int_0^{3 - x}\int_0^{9-3 x-3 y}\,x + 2 y\,dz\,dy\,dx. Integrating with respect to z, M = \int_0^3\int_0^{3 - x} (x + 2 y)(9-3 x-3 y)\,dy\,dx so that M = \int_0^3\int_0^{3 - x} -3 x^2 + 9 x - 3 x y - 6 x y + 18 y - 6 y^2\,dy\,dx. Then, integrating with respect to y, M = \int_0^3 (-3 x^2 + 9 x)(3 - x) + \frac12(18 - 9 x)(3 - x)^2 - 2 (3 - x)^3\,dx. Expanding the these terms, we have M = \int_0^3 \frac{1}{2} x^3 + 0 x^2 + \frac{-27}{2} x + 27\, dx = \frac{243}{8}.
